item.title: This house trumpets its history in the face of gentrification. Now it's a landmark
item.description: A house in San Francisco covered in the painted faces of Latin rock artists was formally landmarked by the city. Its neighborhood has seen skyrocketing home prices and decades of redevelopment.

item.title: Judge says Pentagon's measures against Anthropic were 'illegal and baseless'
item.description: A judge issued a written order Thursday night that the Pentagon acted illegally by punishing the AI company for its criticism of the Department of Defense's views on AI use. The government is expected to fight the ruling.

item.title: Some states are allowing lawsuits against federal agents. Is it a viable option?
item.description: Trump administration officials say federal agents have "total immunity," but a number of states have passed laws allowing them to be sued. But is it a viable option for those seeking accountability?

item.title: NDAs are hiding data center deals, drawing ire from locals — and attention from lawmakers
item.description: Nondisclosure agreements covered up negotiations between a tech company and several local and state officials, surprising local residents. It's a tactic used around the country in data center deals.
